story: As an engineer, I want tabs (Decision, Routing & DFM, Glass Box, Compare, History) and a Role Lens so that I can view the same report through my role's landing lens without anything being walled off.

Glass Box and Compare tabs show EmptyState ('No cost breakdown yet' / 'Nothing to compare yet') until a cost report exists. 'New part' resets all state back to the dropzone.

story: As a manufacturing engineer, I want DFM findings linked to the 3D part so that clicking a face or a blocker highlights the exact geometry.
expected: On the Routing tab, clicking a mesh face that belongs to an issue's affected_faces_sample selects that issue and highlights its faces in a severity-mapped hex color (ghosting the rest); selecting an issue in the list highlights its faces. Highlighting a process with no geometry-linked faces raises a toast 'No geometry-linked faces reported for <process>'.

story: As a cost engineer, I want to bind a shop profile, override rates, and save scenarios so that estimates use real calibrated numbers I can recall.
expected: GET /api/proxy/shops populates bindable shop profiles; selecting one re-runs POST /validate/cost with shop=<id> and toasts 'Calibrating to <name>…'. Applying an override or cavity count re-costs server-side with overrides JSON; 'Clear overrides' resets them. 'Save as scenario' stores a session-local chip (label = shop · overrides · qty) whose click recalls those options and re-costs; scenarios are lost on reset.

story: As a user, I want honest failure states so that a broken mesh or server error tells me what to do instead of a blank screen.
expected: A 400 with code GEOMETRY_INVALID from POST /validate/cost renders the CostGeometryInvalidCard (reason + measured geometry) and a 'Geometry invalid' badge instead of a generic error. story: As an engineer, I want unit-ambiguity warnings and a lineage Inspector so that I can trust and trace the numbers.
expected: report.unit_warnings render in a persistent UnitWarningBanner until the user confirms mm vs inch and re-costs (re-cost re-runs BOTH cost and DFM with the declared units). The collapsible DecisionInspector anchors to the make-now stable-quantity estimate and exposes Lineage/Governance/Sources/Audit tabs (defaults to Sources for the cost role); overrides applied from it trigger a real server re-cost.

feature: History tab: scenarios, copy summary, durable artifact

When the authed cost route persisted the decision (report.saved present and cost-persist UI flag on), a CostArtifactBar offers open/PDF/JSON/CSV/share actions against /cost-decisions/{id} endpoints.

story: As an invited teammate, I want opening my invite link to redeem the token so that I join the organization with the intended role.
expected: On mount, POST /api/proxy/orgs/invites/accept {token}. Missing token → 'Invite token missing.' 401/403 → 'Log in as the invited account.' with a login link whose next returns to /orgs/accept?token=…. Success → 'Invitation accepted.' showing org_role and whether membership was created vs 'already a member; invite consumed without changing your role', plus an 'Open ProofShape' → /verify. Other errors show the backend detail; unreachable server shows 'Could not reach ProofShape.'

story: As an analyst, I upload a ZIP of CAD files (optionally with a manifest CSV and webhook) so the whole set is analyzed as one batch.
expected: With a valid ZIP and role>=analyst, returns 202 with batch_id, status, and status_url=/api/v1/batch/{ulid}; items are extracted and enqueued via arq; webhook_secret is never echoed back. Missing both file and direct_upload_id returns 400 BATCH_INPUT_REQUIRED; providing both returns 400 BATCH_INPUT_CONFLICT.

story: As an analyst, if I pass s3_bucket/s3_prefix/manifest_url I get an honest not-implemented error instead of a doomed pending batch.
expected: Any of s3_bucket, s3_prefix, or manifest_url present returns 501 with code S3_INPUT_UNSUPPORTED and a doc_url, before any Batch row is created. This is EXPECTED behavior, not a bug.

story: As an analyst, I choose job_type=dfm or cost and get clear errors for invalid or disabled modes.
expected: job_type outside {dfm,cost} returns 422 INVALID_JOB_TYPE. job_type=cost with BATCH_COST_ENABLED off (default on) returns 501 BATCH_COST_NOT_ENABLED — an expected honest gate. Invalid cost-manifest rows return 400 INVALID_COST_MANIFEST at create time.

feature: Upload guards: size caps, concurrency, SSRF
story: As an operator, oversized or dangerous batch inputs are rejected before work is created.
expected: Declared Content-Length or streamed ZIP over BATCH_MAX_ZIP_BYTES returns 413; manifest over cap returns 413 BATCH_MANIFEST_TOO_LARGE; concurrency_limit outside 1-12 returns 422 INVALID_BATCH_CONCURRENCY; webhook_url resolving to internal ranges returns 400 webhook_url_rejected (SSRF guard); bad/zip-bomb archives return 400 without orphaned batches.

story: As an analyst, I create a batch from a completed direct_upload_id, and a repeated POST or queue outage never loses or duplicates work.
expected: direct_upload_id path locks and attaches the org-scoped upload; a repeated POST after a lost response returns the original batch (idempotent recovery). If the job queue is down, returns 503 BATCH_ENQUEUE_FAILED with accepted_batch info; a fresh batch is marked failed and its pending items terminalized to skipped so progress reads agree.

story: As a viewer, I list my org's batches newest-first with cursor pagination.
expected: Role>=viewer; results filtered to Batch.org_id == caller's org (never leaks other orgs); returns per-batch status plus completed/failed/skipped item counts, next_cursor, and has_more; limit capped at 100.

story: As a viewer, I poll a batch's progress and page through its items filtered by status.
expected: Progress returns durable item-state counters; unknown or other-org batch returns 404 (never 403). Items endpoint verifies org ownership first (404 otherwise), supports status filter and cursor (limit<=200), and returns per-item filename, status, analysis_id, DFM result fields, error_message, duration_ms.

story: As a viewer, I download batch results as CSV once the batch is finished.
expected: Org-scoped lookup (404 otherwise). Batch not in completed/failed state returns 400 'Batch not yet completed'; otherwise streams text/csv with Content-Disposition attachment filename batch_{id}_results.csv, columns varying by job_type.

story: As an analyst, I cancel an in-flight batch and no items stay stuck pending.
expected: Role>=analyst, org-scoped with row lock (404 otherwise). A batch already completed/failed/cancelled returns 409. Success sets status=cancelled, stamps completed_at, terminalizes all unfinished items to skipped, and returns {batch_id, status:cancelled}.

feature: Corpus list and detail with label overlay
story: As a local single operator (LABELING_ENABLED=1), I browse corpus parts with their manifest metadata and resolved labels.
expected: Routes exist ONLY when LABELING_ENABLED=1 (404 otherwise — expected production behavior); deliberately unauthenticated (localhost tool). List returns offset/limit pages with labeled/unlabeled counts, per-part metadata, process_family_guess, resolved label (exact labeler or majority), and mesh_url; unlabeled_only filters. Detail returns the manifest record plus all effective labels; unknown part_id returns 404.

story: As the local labeler, I fetch a part's STL for the viewer straight from local disk.
expected: Returns FileResponse model/stl with ETag and Cache-Control for a manifest part; part_id not in manifest, a rel_path escaping CORPUS_ROOT (traversal), or a missing file each return 404 with distinct logged reasons. Nothing leaves the machine.

story: As the local labeler, I record one process-family label per part; my latest label wins without erasing history.
expected: part_id not in manifest returns 404; label outside the 6-key ontology (additive, subtractive, injection_molding, sheet_metal, casting, unsure_other) returns 422. Success appends a JSONL record (never mutates prior lines) with labeler resolved from body > X-Labeler header > LABELER env > 'local', and returns {ok, part_id, label, labeler, ts}.

story: As the local labeler, I see how much of the corpus is labeled and by whom.
expected: Returns total_parts, labeled, unlabeled, per_label_counts across the full ontology (zero-filled), per_guess_counts, and the sorted labeler list; optional ?labeler= scopes resolution to that labeler's records.

story: As a viewer, I list my org's Design Studio projects and open one with its current revision.
expected: Role>=viewer, rate-limited 120/hour; list returns up to `limit` (1-100) serialized (project, current revision) pairs scoped to the caller's org. Get returns 404 for unknown or other-org design.

story: As an analyst who is an org member, I submit a name + parametric DesignPlan and get an async generation job producing immutable STEP/STL artifacts.
expected: Requires analyst role AND org member (require_role_and_org_role) plus open write kill-switch; body is strictly validated (extra fields forbidden, name 1-120 chars). Success returns 202 with serialized design, job_id, and poll_url; caller with no org gets 403. If the job queue is down, returns 503 DESIGN_ENQUEUE_FAILED with the persisted design still included in the body.

story: As an analyst, I type a natural-language prompt (max 500 chars) and get a structured DesignPlan suggestion without creating anything.
expected: Requires analyst+org-member role; synchronous, no DB write; returns the interpreter's plan output for the prompt. Empty or over-length prompt fails validation (422).

story: As an analyst, I add a new plan revision to a design and read back the immutable revision history.
expected: Create returns 202 with new revision + job_id; 404 for unknown/other-org design and 409 'The current revision is still generating' while a build is in flight; queue outage returns 503 DESIGN_ENQUEUE_FAILED. Revision list returns current_revision plus all serialized revisions; revision_no < 1 or unknown returns 404.

story: As an analyst org-member, I archive a design I no longer need.
expected: Kill-switch gated; returns 204 on success; 404 for unknown/other-org design; 409 'A generating design cannot be archived' while its revision is still building.

story: As a viewer, I stream the STL preview or download the STEP file for the current or a specific revision.
expected: Org-scoped; streams model/stl inline or model/step attachment with sanitized filename; STEP responses carry Cache-Control: private, no-store and an X-Geometry-SHA256 header with the revision's geometry hash. Not-yet-succeeded revision returns 409 'Design artifact is not ready'/'unavailable'; deleted blob returns 410; unknown design 404.

story: As a viewer, I see which SAP/PLM/quote connectors exist and their honest mode (offline_csv vs sandbox_api — no live credentials pretended).
expected: Role>=viewer; returns the static connector list with id, mode (offline_csv or sandbox_api), and metadata; no org data involved.

story: As an org admin, I register and list connector credential profiles for my org.
expected: Requires OrgRole.admin; caller without an org gets 403. POST validates connector_id/label/base_url/auth_type lengths and returns 201 with the serialized profile (secret material not echoed raw); GET lists the org's profiles optionally filtered by connector_id.

story: As an org admin, I inspect a stored profile, run a connectivity probe, and revoke it.
expected: All org-scoped to the admin's org (other-org profile not retrievable). Probe returns a probe result object without performing live-credentialed writes; DELETE marks the profile revoked and returns the updated serialized profile (200).

feature: Offline CSV dry-run / import with run ledger
story: As an analyst, I upload a connector CSV export to dry-run it through the real parsers, or actually import it, with durable run evidence either way.
expected: mode=dry_run parses only; mode=import executes the matching importer and is blocked when the write kill-switch is closed; any other mode returns 400. Empty upload returns 400; CSV over INTEGRATION_IMPORT_MAX_MB (default 10MB) returns 413; unknown connector 404; non-UTF-8 CSV 400. Success persists an org-stamped integration_runs ledger row (raw bytes hashed+counted, not stored) and returns the serialized run with imported/updated counts (0 in dry_run).

story: As a viewer, I audit past connector runs for my org and open one run's evidence.
expected: Role>=viewer, org-scoped (403 with no org). List is cursor-paginated (limit<=100) with connector_id and status filters (invalid status returns 400); detail returns 404 for unknown/other-org run.

story: As an analyst, I bundle saved cost-decision artifacts into a local RFQ evidence package for a supplier (no send, no marketplace).
expected: Kill-switch gated, role>=analyst, org required (403 otherwise). Empty decision_ids returns 400; more than MAX_ITEMS returns 400; any decision not found in the caller's org returns 404. Success returns 201 with the serialized package including items; include_raw_cad optionally embeds source CAD.

story: As a viewer, I list my org's RFQ packages and open one with its line items.
expected: Role>=viewer; list returns up to limit (1-100) org-scoped packages; detail includes items and returns 404 'RFQ package not found.' for unknown or other-org package.

story: As a viewer, I download the package as a ZIP (supplier brief, line-items CSV, decision evidence, optional CAD).
expected: Org-scoped (404 otherwise); builds the ZIP on demand and returns application/zip with a sanitized attachment filename '{title}-{ulid}.zip'.

story: As any authenticated user, I check whether image-to-3D is actually enabled before my browser accepts images.
expected: Role>=viewer; returns available, can_submit (true only for analyst+), effective_backend, customer_data_egress/requires_egress_acknowledgement flags, an honest human message for each state (disabled / third-party egress / in-deployment), and an accuracy_notice that meshes are estimates, plus verify_path fallback.

feature: Image-to-mesh submit with honest 501 + egress opt-in gate
story: As an analyst, I upload 1-4 images with a ULID Idempotency-Key to reconstruct a mesh — and if no backend is available I get an honest refusal, never a silent third-party egress.
expected: With no local model and no explicit remote opt-in (RECONSTRUCTION_BACKEND=remote / RECONSTRUCTION_ALLOW_REMOTE_EGRESS=1), returns 501 RECONSTRUCTION_UNAVAILABLE — EXPECTED default behavior. A remote-egress backend without the X-Reconstruction-Egress-Acknowledged header returns 428. Otherwise: image count outside 1-4 or invalid images return 400, idempotency conflict 409, queue outage 503 RECONSTRUCTION_ENQUEUE_FAILED (retryable), success 202 with job_id and poll_url /api/v1/jobs/{ulid}.

story: As a viewer who owns the job, I download the reconstructed STL once the job completes.
expected: Ownership-scoped; streams application/sla with attachment filename reconstructed_{job_id}.stl; returns 404 when the job is unknown, not the caller's, or not complete.

story: As an analyst, I persist real cost/quote data (with provenance and stand_in honesty flags) for my org; as a viewer I read it back.
expected: Create: kill-switch gated, analyst, 403 without org, 400 on invalid payload (non-positive cost etc.); last-write-wins dedup on (part_id, process, quantity, shop); emits groundtruth.ingested audit event; source_type synthetic/seed/demo/stand_in is forced to stand_in=True and can never validate. Reads: viewer, org-scoped; detail returns 404 for other-org record.

story: As an analyst, I trigger recalibration over my org's records to refresh measured cost confidence intervals — but only when there is enough REAL data.
expected: Kill-switch gated, analyst, tight rate limit (10/hour). With fewer than MIN_REAL_RECORDS real (non-stand-in) records, returns 422 naming n_real, n_records, and min_real instead of emitting a calibration from synthetic data — EXPECTED honest refusal. Otherwise returns the recalibration summary including whether the band is validated (True only from real held-out residuals).

feature: Bulk CSV import with honest partial success
story: As an analyst, I download the exact CSV header, then bulk-import historical costs; bad rows are reported per-line, never coerced.
expected: Template returns plain-text CSV header + example (viewer). Import: kill-switch gated, analyst; accepts multipart file OR raw text/csv body; over GROUNDTRUTH_IMPORT_MAX_MB (default 10MB) returns 413 streamed (never buffered unbounded); empty 400; non-UTF-8 400. Always 200 on parseable input with {imported, skipped, total, errors:[{line, reason}]} — even imported=0 with all rows invalid; imported rows go through the same org-scoped create path as real (stand_in=False) unless source_type marks them synthetic.

story: As an operator, my Prometheus scraper reads machine metrics without an API key (private-network scrape by design).
expected: Unauthenticated by design. METRICS_ENABLED=0 returns 404 (expected disable behavior); prometheus-client not installed returns honest 503 'metrics unavailable'; otherwise returns text/plain; version=0.0.4 exposition including HTTP counters/histograms and queue/worker gauges refreshed from ops health (scrape stays 200 even if the DB is momentarily down — stale gauges over a failing endpoint).

story: As a security-conscious operator, metrics never leak ULIDs, filenames, or user data through labels.
expected: MetricsMiddleware records every request under the matched route TEMPLATE (e.g. /api/v1/batch/{batch_id}); unmatched requests collapse to a single __unmatched__ label; cost-decision outcomes are clamped to {ok, geometry_invalid, error}; status gauges are bucketed to fixed status sets with 'other' overflow. Requesting /api/v1/batch/SOME-ULID then scraping /metrics shows the template label, never the raw ULID.

story: As a viewer, I see a paginated grid of my org's parts with recommended route, unit cost, DFM findings, provenance posture, and Drafted/Costed state so I can browse the portfolio without joining raw endpoints.
expected: Requires viewer role; rows built only from caller's org (resolve_org; no membership = empty grid, never cross-org). Offset pagination (page/page_size<=100) with consistent total; facets state/route/has_findings applied before pagination; invalid state value = 400. Response includes facets summary over full org catalog, filters echo, and honest truncated flag when scan cap exceeded.

story: As a viewer with a huge inventory, I can walk the whole uncapped catalog with keyset pagination over the materialized part-summary projection.
expected: keyset=true returns {rows, next_cursor}; passing next_cursor back walks pages; facet filters do not apply. Undecodable cursor = 400 'invalid cursor', never 500. Cold projection with real parts: first page (no cursor) falls back read-only to legacy capped catalog with cold_projection:true and truncated flag.

story: As a viewer, I see my org's Costed parts ranked by engine-computed redesign savings with an honest posture aggregate so I can prioritize redesigns.
expected: Viewer role; org-scoped (no org = empty roll-up). savings is always a delta of two persisted engine numbers; parts with no signal carry savings:null + reason; parts with no cost decision excluded (excluded_no_cost_count); validated copied from confidence band, never set here. $/year figures appear only when user-declared annual_volume exists (context_note added when programs declared); truncated scan adds a note. Interactive rate limit 600/hour.

story: As a viewer, I see how many of my org's parts are makeable / needs_review / unknown per process so I can triage a legacy pile at portfolio scale.
expected: Viewer role; org-scoped; empty org returns zeroed summary (not error). Buckets are exhaustive and mutually exclusive (sum to total); parts with no analysis are 'unknown', never assumed makeable. Uses SQL GROUP BY over part_summaries projection; cold projection with real parts falls back read-only to legacy capped fold with truncated:true + note. Programs grouping present only when user-declared programs exist.

story: As a viewer, I see how many parts are makeable on owned equipment vs. outside vs. blocked by a capability gap, and can drill into each bucket, so I can plan in-house work.
expected: Viewer role; org-scoped; rollup counts 6 buckets from stored Phase-C verdicts, never recomputed. Invalid bucket name = 400 listing valid buckets; bucket drill-down returns keyset {rows, next_cursor} with per-row makeability {verdict, stale, gap}; bad cursor = 400. Stale verdicts counted and flagged (stale_note), never hidden; cold projection with real parts adds cold_projection:true + note; zero evaluated parts adds evaluation_note.

story: As a viewer, I see which single machine acquisition would unlock the most blocked parts so I can justify equipment purchases.
expected: Viewer role; org-scoped; ranking is a GROUP BY over stored (unlock_process, unlock_gate) gap data — no acquisition dollar cost ever fabricated (basis_note states this). Parts blocked by multiple constraints reported separately in summary.blocked_by_multiple_constraints, never folded in. ?process= (optionally &gate=) returns keyset drill-down of unlocked parts; bad cursor = 400; stale entries flagged; empty ranking with zero blocked adds explanatory note.

story: As a viewer, I list my org's saved cost decisions (cursor-paginated, filterable by process/date) and open one to see the full immutable result_json with governance state.
expected: Viewer role; list is org-scoped via caller_org_subquery; ULID cursor pagination with has_more/next_cursor; invalid ISO created_after/before = 400. Detail returns full envelope incl. mesh_hash (private source identity), share_url, governance fields; a decision in another org = 404 (never 403, existence never leaks).

story: As a viewer, I get a structured diff of two owned decisions (unit cost by qty, make/tooling process, crossover, driver deltas) to evaluate alternatives.
expected: Viewer role; exactly two comma-separated ids required else 400; each id must resolve in caller's org else 404. Response compares recommended unit cost per quantity with delta and pct, plus process/crossover diffs.

story: As an analyst, I record the four-way outcome (inhouse/outside/acquire/redesign) or withdraw it with null, without altering the engine artifact.
expected: Analyst role; org-scoped 404. Invalid disposition = 400 (422 via Literal at router); note >1000 chars = 400. Recording 'inhouse' while the selected route is DFM-blocked = 409 (fail closed). Any real change reopens an existing approval; identical repeat PUT is idempotent (no timestamp rewrite, no duplicate audit). result_json remains byte-identical; audit event emitted.

story: As an analyst, I sign off a saved decision (optional note ≤1000 chars) or reopen its approval, leaving the saved artifact immutable.
expected: Analyst role; org-scoped 404. Approve sets approval_status=approved with approver id/timestamp/trimmed note; DELETE resets to unreviewed and clears approver fields. Response returns governance fields incl. time-aware is_stale (future stale_at not stale until effective instant).

story: As a viewer, I download the cost-report PDF of a saved decision for offline review.
expected: Viewer role; org-scoped (service resolves via user_id, 404 for foreign decisions). Returns application/pdf with sanitized attachment filename; PDF generated or fetched from cache by cost_pdf_service.

story: As a viewer, I export the decision's raw result_json (plus governance block) or an estimates/line-items/confidence CSV for external analysis.
expected: Viewer role; org-scoped 404. JSON export = result_json merged with governance fields, attachment Content-Disposition with sanitized filename stem; CSV export = build_estimates_csv over result_json + governance, text/csv attachment.

story: As an analyst, I generate a public /s/cost/{short_id} link for a decision and can revoke it so the link 404s immediately.
expected: Analyst role; org-scoped 404. POST is idempotent — an existing share returns the same short id; sets is_public=true. DELETE clears share_short_id and is_public, returns 'Share revoked'.

story: As an anonymous link recipient, I view a shared cost decision sanitized of owner PII so the owner can share evidence safely.
expected: No auth; 404 when short_id unknown or share revoked (is_public false). Response is allow-listed — excludes user_id, api_key_id, mesh_hash, params_hash, ids — while decision content (estimates, provenance, confidence band) is verbatim. Headers: X-Robots-Tag noindex and Cache-Control private,no-store; rate-limited 120/hour.

story: As a viewer, I fetch static MachineProfile templates (provenance 'catalog_template') to prefill a declaration, and the exact CSV header for a bulk import.
expected: Viewer role; no org required for /catalog. Templates are editable prefills, never claimed as the org's machines. Template endpoint returns plaintext header (required column process; optional name/count/max_workpiece_kg/hourly_rate_usd/capital_frac/materials/material_thickness_map/capabilities/notes) plus an example row.

story: As an analyst, I declare (upsert) my org's shop-level secondary-op set; as a viewer I read it back (empty ops when unset).
expected: GET viewer / PUT analyst; both 403 when caller has no org. PUT gated by kill switch; idempotent per org; a malformed op value or non-positive limit = 400, never coerced. A successful PUT marks the org's makeability projection stale in the same transaction.

story: As an analyst, I bulk-import owned machines from CSV and get an honest partial-success summary.
expected: Analyst role + kill switch; 403 no org. Accepts multipart file or raw text/csv body; streamed with size cap (MACHINE_IMPORT_MAX_MB, default 10MB) = 413 on overflow, 400 empty or non-UTF-8. Strict parse: valid rows INSERTED (append, no natural key), bad rows reported per-line; returns 200 {imported, skipped, total, errors:[{line,reason}]}. Any import marks makeability projection stale.

story: As an analyst I declare one owned machine; as a viewer I list the org's machines (keyset, id ASC) and read one by id.
expected: Create: analyst + kill switch, 403 no org, malformed capability field = 400 never coerced, 201 with provenance:'user' payload, audit event machine.created, marks projection stale. List/get: viewer, org-scoped; foreign or unknown id = 404 'no such machine in org'.

story: As an analyst, I patch only the supplied machine fields (merged result re-validated) or delete a machine from the org registry.
expected: Analyst + kill switch; 403 no org; 404 when machine not in caller's org; 400 on malformed field. Both mutations mark the makeability projection stale in the same txn and emit machine.updated/machine.deleted audit events; delete returns {deleted:true, id}.

story: As a viewer, I list my org's materials-catalog versions (newest first, with flag_enabled) and open one with its full payload.
expected: Viewer role; org-scoped; caller with no org gets empty versions list (list) and 404 (detail). Detail includes payload; foreign-org version = 404. flag_enabled reflects MATERIAL_LIBRARY_ENABLED.

story: As a viewer, I see whether the engine is actually overlaying a governed material catalog right now, so I never mistake an authored-but-unused catalog for a live one.
expected: Viewer role. using_governed true only when flag on AND a published catalog is in effect; otherwise source='base_rate_table_material_prices' and payload null. Response always carries provenance:'default' and validated:false — declared prices are never validated.

story: As an org admin, I create a draft catalog (blank, from payload, or copied from an existing version) and edit its name/note/payload while still draft.
expected: Requires org-admin (require_org_role); 400 when caller has no org. Invalid payload = 400; editing a non-draft = 409; unknown version / foreign org = 404. Returns serialized version with payload.

story: As an org admin, I discard an unwanted draft outright, or archive a superseded published version — but never delete the audit trail or strand the live overlay.
expected: Org-admin; 404 unknown version. DELETE only works on drafts — published/archived = 409 (audit trail). Archive only works on published versions (409 otherwise) and the version currently in effect cannot be archived (409).

story: As an org admin, I publish a draft with an effective date so the costing engine overlays it from that instant.
expected: Org-admin; only drafts publishable (already-published = 409); effective_from in the past = 400; publishing closes the previously open version's effective_to (no overlap). Side effects in same txn: org cost decisions marked stale (reason material_library_published:vN, stale_at=effective_from) and library.version_published audit event.

story: As a viewer, I list my org's rate-card versions, read one with payload, and see whether the engine is actually using a governed card vs. hardcoded RATE_CARD_V0.
expected: Viewer role; org-scoped; no org = empty list / 404 detail. /effective: using_governed true only when RATE_LIBRARY_ENABLED and a published card in effect, else source='default_rate_card_v0'; always provenance:'default', validated:false.

story: As an org admin, I draft a rate card (default table or copy of a version), edit it while draft, discard drafts, and archive superseded published versions.
expected: Org-admin; 400 no org. Payload validated on create/edit (400 on invalid); edit/discard non-draft = 409; archive non-published = 409; archiving the currently-in-effect card = 409 (would strand the engine); unknown/foreign version = 404.

story: As a viewer, I see exactly which leaf keys changed between two of my org's rate-card versions (path, from, to) to review a governance change.
expected: Viewer role; both versions must exist in caller's org else 404 (never cross-tenant). Only genuinely changed leaf keys listed; unchanged keys never appear; response includes serialized from/to metadata.

story: As an org admin, I publish a draft rate card with an effective date so the engine reads it as the base default table.
expected: Org-admin; draft-only (409 otherwise); past effective_from = 400; timeline never overlaps (prior open version closed). Marks org cost decisions stale (reason rate_library_published:vN) and emits library.version_published audit event in same txn.

story: As a viewer, I list my org's per-slug shop-profile versions and read one with payload, replacing the read-only flat-file profiles.
expected: Viewer role; org-scoped; no org = empty list / 404 detail; foreign version = 404; flag_enabled reflects SHOP_LIBRARY_ENABLED. Governed profile is declared calibration bound as SHOP provenance — never validated/certified.

story: As an org admin, I draft a shop profile under a slug, edit it while draft, discard drafts, archive superseded published versions, and publish with an effective date.
expected: Org-admin; 400 no org; invalid body = 400; edit/discard non-draft = 409; archive: only published and not currently-in-effect-for-its-slug (409); publish is draft-only with no past effective_from, marks org decisions stale (reason shop_profile_published:slug:vN) and emits a library.version_published audit event.

story: As a viewer, I read the user-declared business context (program, parent assembly, units per parent, annual volume, service environment, BOM linkage) for a part in my org.
expected: Viewer role; org-scoped — no org or no declared row = 404 'no declared context for part' (cross-tenant read also 404). Response carries provenance:'user' — declared, never inferred from the mesh.

story: As an analyst, I declare or update a part's context idempotently on (org, mesh_hash) and get back the recomputed portfolio row so the UI patches state without refetching the rate-limited portfolio.
expected: Analyst role; 400 when no org; non-positive units_per_parent/annual_volume (or invalid service_environment / BOM fields) = 400, never coerced. Response is provenance:'user' and includes portfolio_delta computed after commit via the same build_portfolio path as GET /catalog/portfolio (byte-identical to a refetch). Nothing flips validated or fabricates demand.

story: As an analyst, I upload a STEP/IGES assembly and persist its real derived parent->child edge tree (source 'assembly_step') so rollups use measured instance counts.
expected: Analyst + kill switch + org limits; 403 no org; upload capped (BOM_ASSEMBLY_MAX_MB, default 256MB) = 413; empty upload = 400. Reuses /validate/assembly extraction (security gate + 400s); idempotent per (org, assembly_key) — re-ingest replaces the tree; assembly_key defaults to filename; single-part file persists 0 edges with an honest note, never a fabricated hierarchy. Returns {assembly_key, edges, roots, source}.

story: As an analyst, I onboard a parent_ref,child_ref,qty_per_parent BOM (CSV/JSON, file or raw body) against an assembly_key; the template endpoint gives me the exact header.
expected: Analyst + kill switch; 403 no org; size cap 413 (BOM_IMPORT_MAX_MB default 10MB); empty body = 400; missing assembly_key (query/form/filename) = 400; non-UTF-8 = 400; > BOM_MAX_ROWS = 413. Strict parse: valid edges persisted (re-onboard replaces tree, source 'bom_csv'); malformed rows skipped and reported as errors:[{line,reason}]. Template (viewer) returns header + example row.

story: As a viewer, I trace a part child->root with the rolled-up multiplier and read the persisted edge list for an assembly key.
expected: Viewer role; 403 no org; org-scoped so another org's tree is invisible. Missing tree or child_ref not in it = 200 with has_tree=false, empty chains, rolled_up_multiplier=null — never 500 or fabricated ancestry; shared components return every root-path in ancestry_paths and the SUMMED multiplier. Tree read returns {assembly_key, edges, roots, has_tree} with empty edges (not 404) for an absent tree.

story: As an analyst, I bulk-import my org's declared parts manifest (SAP/Excel CSV, usually without geometry) with honest partial success; the template gives the exact columns.
expected: Analyst + kill switch + org limits; 403 no org. Multipart file or raw text/csv; streamed cap (MANIFEST_IMPORT_MAX_MB default 10MB) = 413; empty = 400; non-UTF-8 = 400. Valid rows UPSERTED on (org_id, part_id) last-write-wins; bad rows reported per-line; fully-invalid file still 200 with imported=0 + errors. Returns {imported, updated, skipped, total, errors}. Template (viewer): required part_id, optional declared metadata columns.

story: As a viewer, I page through my org's declared manifest (keyset, part_id ASC) and see the coverage headline: total declared parts, by_program rollup, and how many have uploaded geometry.
expected: Viewer role; 403 when caller has no org; org-scoped (one org's manifest never leaks). List returns {parts, next_cursor} with next_cursor null only on the final page and bounded limit. Coverage counts with_geometry/without_geometry by exact normalized-stem match against the same org's uploaded analyses — an honest count, never inferred.

feature: Full DFM validation of uploaded CAD
story: As an API engineer, I want to upload an STL/STEP/IGES part and get full manufacturing-validation results (geometry, segments, features, universal issues, per-process scores with standards citations, priority fixes) so I can judge manufacturability.
expected: Requires API key with analyst role (401 no key, 403 viewer-only), kill-switch dep and 60/hour;500/day rate limit (429). 200 returns geometry summary, process_scores ranked, best_process with honest 'best_process_basis: geometry-manufacturability; material not declared' label; optional ?include_thickness=true adds wall_thickness_map; ?units=inch scales mesh x25.4 once. Errors: 400 unknown rule_pack/units/process, bad magic bytes, unsupported suffix, empty file; 413 over MAX_UPLOAD_MB (100MB default); 501 STEP without gmsh; 504 parse/analysis over ANALYSIS_TIMEOUT_SEC. Persists analysis row + usage_event via analysis_service (dedup by mesh hash).

story: As an API engineer, I want to request SAM-3D segmentation with my validation so a background job computes it while I get the synchronous result immediately.
expected: Same auth as /validate. Returns 202 with {analysis_id, job_id, poll_url: /api/v1/jobs/{ulid}, result} after persisting the analysis, saving the mesh blob, and creating an idempotent sam3d job row. If Redis enqueue fails, returns structured 503 SAM3D_ENQUEUE_FAILED with retryable:true and the committed job_id retained for safe retry.

feature: Browser-renderable GLB preview of real tessellated shell
story: As a frontend engineer, I want a decimated GLB of the uploaded part's real tessellated shell so STEP/IGES parts render as themselves in WebGL instead of a bounding box.
expected: Analyst role required (401/403), 120/hour;1000/day limit (429). 200 returns model/gltf-binary bytes with headers X-Mesh-Original-Faces, X-Mesh-Preview-Faces, X-Mesh-Decimated, X-Mesh-Source, Cache-Control: no-store; decimates above PREVIEW_MESH_TARGET_FACES (50k default). Errors: 400 bad file/magic/export failure, 413 oversize, 501 no gmsh, 504 parse timeout. Zero-egress, nothing persisted; single-flight cache dedupes concurrent parses of the same bytes.

story: As an API engineer, I want to ingest a multi-solid STEP/IGES assembly and get per-part meshes, world positions, product tree, and optionally per-part DFM + should-cost + interference analysis.
expected: Analyst role, 60/hour;500/day. format=json returns AssemblyModel dict (single-solid files classified single_part, limits/boundaries fields state AP203 caveats); format=glb returns combined GLB with X-Assembly-Kind/Parts headers; format=analysis validates material_class/region/assemblies_per_year first (400 on bad values) and returns model + analysis with honest 'N of M analyzed' degrade under time budget. Errors: 400 native CAD (.SLDASM/.prt) with specific message, 400 non-STEP/IGES suffix or bad magic, 413 oversize, 501 no gmsh, 504 timeout. Nothing persisted.

story: As an API engineer, I want a fast pass/fail check running only universal checks (no per-process analysis) so I can triage uploads cheaply.
expected: Analyst role (401/403), 60/hour;500/day (429). 200 returns quick-analysis result from analysis_service.run_quick_analysis; 400 empty/bad file, 413 over size limit. Persists via the analysis service path.

story: As an anonymous evaluator, I want to run full DFM analysis without an API key so I can try the product with my CAD never persisted.
expected: No auth, tight 10/hour rate limit (429). 200 returns same response shape as /validate plus demo:true; no persistence, no DB writes. 413 (not 400) when STL exceeds DEMO_MAX_TRIANGLES (500k default) either declared or post-tessellation; 400 bad file/magic/unknown process; 504 on timeout. Optional include_thickness works as on /validate.

story: As a buyer/engineer, I want an explainable should-cost decision for my part across quantities, with shop calibration, rate overrides, owned processes, tolerance and units declarations, so I can decide make-vs-buy with provenance-tagged assumptions.
expected: Analyst role (401/403), 60/hour;500/day (429). Fail-fast 400s: bad qty (max 6 values, 1..10M), unknown complexity/material_class/region/tolerance_class/units/shop/process id, overrides not a finite-number JSON object (max 64 keys) or unknown override key. 200 returns decision dict with drivers/assumptions provenance (DEFAULT/USER/SHOP), optional 'uncertainty' band (COST_ENSEMBLE_ENABLED, validated=true only from real residuals else honest validated=false), 'identity' (org retrieval suggestion or null), and 'saved': {id, url} pointer when COST_PERSIST_ENABLED (persist failure degrades gracefully and records a usage_events failure row). Broken geometry returns structured 400 GEOMETRY_INVALID with geometry summary + doc_url, never 500; 504 on compute timeout. Side effects: source artifact + costable STL saved for the org, cost decision row persisted, structured cost_estimate log event, metrics recorded.

story: As an anonymous evaluator, I want the same should-cost decision without an API key so I can evaluate costing while my CAD stays local and ephemeral.
expected: No auth, 240/hour limit (429). Identical validation and 400/413/501/504 error paths as /validate/cost, same Sigma=unit_cost and provenance invariants, but no persistence, no saved pointer, no ensemble uncertainty (authed-only), identity:null always, no owned_processes param. Response never includes org-calibrated bands (validated stays false / assumption-band only).

story: As an engineer, I want the server to attempt mesh repair on my upload and show before/after analysis so I can see whether repair fixes DFM blockers.
expected: Analyst role (401/403), 60/hour;500/day (429). 400 on unknown rule_pack (validated before reading bytes), empty/bad file; 413 oversize. 200 returns repair_service.repair_mesh result (before/after comparison). Uses same rule_pack/process filters as /validate.

feature: Reference catalogs (rule packs, processes, materials, machines)
story: As an API user, I want to list the industry rule packs, supported processes, materials, and machine profiles so I can populate valid request parameters and UI pickers.
expected: Viewer role suffices (401 without key), 60/hour;500/day (429). Each returns 200 with a static catalog: rule_packs (name/version/description/override+mandatory counts), processes, materials (min_wall_mm, tensile_mpa, cost_per_kg_usd), machines (build_volume_mm, min_layer_mm, materials). No side effects, no DB.

story: As a buyer, I want to list per-shop calibration profiles so I can pass a shop id to /validate/cost and re-cost against that shop's real rates.
expected: Viewer role (401 no key), 60/hour;500/day (429). 200 returns {shops:[{id, name, region, source}]} read from the local backend/data/shop_profiles store (no network); profiles that fail to load are skipped with a warning. The ids are the accepted values for the cost route's shop field (unknown shop there is 400 listing available ids).

story: As an integrator, I want to discover the direct-upload contract (allowed purpose, size/part limits) without S3 coordinates exposed so I can implement a compliant multipart client.
expected: Analyst role (401/403). 200 returns capability dict for purpose (default batch_zip) incl. max_parts=10000 and max_part_urls_per_response=1000; unknown purpose maps DirectUploadError to its status (400-family) with optional Retry-After header. No side effects.

story: As an integrator, I want to initiate an org-scoped multipart upload with an Idempotency-Key so retries replay the same upload instead of creating duplicates.
expected: Analyst role (401/403); strict body schema (extra fields forbidden -> 422 VALIDATION_ERROR). 201 returns upload_id, presigned part URLs, part_urls_complete flag, idempotent_replay flag, and refresh/complete/abort/status URLs. Service errors (bad purpose/content_type/size over BATCH_MAX_ZIP_BYTES, per-org active-upload and byte caps) map to structured HTTP errors, optionally with Retry-After. Persists a direct_upload row scoped to caller's org.

feature: Multipart upload lifecycle (refresh URLs, complete, abort, status)
story: As an integrator, I want to refresh expiring part URLs, complete the upload with part etags, abort it, and poll its status so I can drive the full multipart lifecycle.
expected: All analyst-role, org/user-scoped: another user's upload id yields the service's not-found error. Refresh rejects >1000 part numbers per call; complete takes {parts:[{part_number, etag}]} and returns the serialized upload (state transition persisted); abort marks it aborted; GET status returns serialized upload plus attached_batch_ulid when a batch consumed it. Legacy aliases POST /multipart/{id}/complete and DELETE /multipart/{id} exist but are hidden from schema. 422 on malformed bodies (extra fields forbidden).

story: As a user, I want to download a rendered PDF report of a past analysis so I can archive or forward it.
expected: Viewer role (401 no key), 60/hour;500/day (429). 200 returns application/pdf bytes with Content-Disposition attachment using a sanitized filename; 404 when the analysis does not exist or is not visible to the caller. PDF is generated on demand or served from cache by pdf_service.

story: As an analyst, I want to create a public short-URL share for my analysis and revoke it later so I can control external visibility.
expected: Analyst role (401/403), 60/hour;500/day (429). POST returns the share record (short id/url) and marks the analysis public (persisted); 404 when the analysis isn't found for this user. DELETE returns {message: 'Share revoked'} and the public link 404s immediately afterward; 404 for unknown/foreign analysis.

story: As a link recipient without an account, I want to view a sanitized shared analysis so the owner can show me results without granting API access.
expected: No auth; IP rate limit 120/hour (429). 200 returns sanitized analysis data with X-Robots-Tag: noindex and Cache-Control: private, no-store headers; 404 for unknown, revoked, or expired short ids.

story: As a viewer, I want to page through my organization's past analyses and open one with its full result and linked cost decisions so I can revisit prior work.
expected: Viewer role (401 no key), 60/hour;500/day (429). List is org-scoped via caller_org_subquery (never leaks other orgs), cursor-paginated by ULID desc (limit 1..100, default 20; 422 outside range), optional verdict filter (pass|issues|fail; invalid values silently ignored); returns {analyses, next_cursor, has_more}. Detail returns full result_json plus is_public/share_url and up to 20 decision_links matched by org+mesh_hash; 404 for unknown or other-org ULIDs.

feature: Async job status polling and result fetch
story: As an API engineer, I want to poll an async job (e.g. SAM-3D) and fetch its result when done so I can complete long-running workflows.
expected: Viewer role (401 no key). Status returns {job_id, status, job_type, timestamps, result_url, error}; result_url is set only when status is done/partial, and error carries {code, message} (JOB_FAILED fallback) when failed. Both endpoints return 404 for non-existent jobs AND other users' jobs (no existence leak); /result also 404s ('Job result not yet available') while the job is queued/running.

story: As an operator, I want a health endpoint that never claims an absent dependency is healthy so my monitors reflect reality.
expected: No auth. 200 {status: ok} only when Postgres probe passes and (when the async tier is expected: real REDIS_URL or RELEASE set, with ASYNC_STRICT_HEALTH=1 default) Redis is reachable; otherwise 503 {status: degraded}. Body always reports real probes: postgres, redis, async{redis, worker: ok|unknown|unavailable, expected}, reconstruction{available, backend, egress}, version, build_id. Worker 'unknown' (no arq heartbeat key) does not gate status unless WORKER_STRICT_HEALTH=1.

feature: Deep dependency health with optional token gate
story: As an operator, I want per-dependency probes (Postgres, Redis, worker heartbeat age, queue depth, object store) so I can diagnose exactly what is degraded.
expected: When DEEP_HEALTH_TOKEN is set (or PRODUCTION_DEEP_HEALTH_AUTH_REQUIRED=1), a missing/wrong X-CadVerify-Health-Token returns 404 'Not found' (hides the endpoint, not 401). Otherwise 200/503 with checks.postgres{ok,error}, checks.redis{ok,expected,configured,error}, checks.worker{state: ok|stale|unknown|unavailable, heartbeat_age_seconds, stale_threshold_seconds}, checks.queue{depth,name}, checks.object_store{ok,expected,backend}; 503 when Postgres down, expected Redis unreachable (strict), strict worker not ok, or expected object store failing healthcheck. Worker state is never fabricated 'ok' without a fresh heartbeat.

feature: Structured error responses with stable codes
story: As an API consumer, I want every error to carry a stable machine-readable code, message, and doc_url so I can handle failures programmatically.
expected: Any HTTPException is wrapped as {code, message, doc_url[, detail]} using the stable map (400 BAD_REQUEST, 401 UNAUTHORIZED, 403 FORBIDDEN, 404 NOT_FOUND, 409 CONFLICT, 413 FILE_TOO_LARGE, 422 VALIDATION_ERROR, 429 RATE_LIMITED, 501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED, 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, 504 ANALYSIS_TIMEOUT). A detail dict already containing 'code' (e.g. GEOMETRY_INVALID, SAM3D_ENQUEUE_FAILED) passes through unchanged with original headers; Pydantic validation failures return 422 VALIDATION_ERROR.

story: As a holder of an old docs link, I want /docs to forward me so that I land on the current API quickstart.
expected: /docs unconditionally issues a Next.js redirect to /developers; no content is rendered at /docs itself.

story: As an analyst, I confirm/correct a part's declared identity so future retrievals carry a human assertion instead of a guess.
expected: Analyst role required; upserts declared_part_id/name/program onto the (org, mesh_hash) corpus row with source='user_confirmed' and emits identity.confirm audit event. 400 if caller has no org, mesh_hash blank, or no declared field supplied; 404 if the mesh has no corpus row in the caller's org (incl. another org's part — never a cross-tenant write, never a fabricated signature). Rate-limited 120/hour.

story: As an analyst, I bulk-upload my org's CAD library (files or ZIP) with an identity mapping so the corpus has real declared identities on day one.
expected: Analyst role + kill-switch open required; 403 if no org. Accepts multipart files and/or ZIP plus optional CSV/JSON mapping; 400 if no files, 413 if >512MB (env PARTS_MASTER_MAX_MB) or over ONBOARD_MAX_FILES cap, 400 if mapping is not UTF-8. Returns honest summary {onboarded, skipped:[{filename,reason}], mapping_errors, library_size} — unparseable files are skipped, never abort the batch; missing names onboard bare geometry with no guessing. Rate-limited 20/hour.

story: As a viewer, I see my org's identity-corpus size and recent entries, and download the mapping CSV contract.
expected: Viewer role required. GET /library returns {library_size, recent:[...]} org-scoped with declared identity only (raw signature vector never emitted); 403 if caller has no org. GET /library/template returns text/csv with header 'filename' (required) + optional part_id/name/program/material_class and needs no org.

story: As an analyst, I create a named org and become its admin.
expected: Analyst role + kill-switch open required; 201 with {org_id, name, slug, org_role:'admin'}; caller's active org is NOT auto-switched. 400 for empty name or name >200 chars. Emits org.created audit event.

story: As a viewer, I list every org I belong to and see which is active.
expected: Viewer role required; returns caller's memberships with the active org flagged; no cross-user data.

story: As a member with a dashboard session, I switch my active org.
expected: Viewer role + kill-switch open; org-bound API keys are refused with 403 {code:'api_key_org_bound'} — only dashboard sessions may switch (keys are permanently org-bound). 403 'not a member of that organization' when switching to an org without membership. Emits org.switched.

story: As an org admin, I manage SAML group-to-role mappings for JIT provisioning in my org.
expected: Org-admin role required (mutations kill-switch gated); mappings are strictly org-scoped — list returns only caller-org rows, delete of another org's mapping fails. POST returns 201 with serialized mapping; both mutations emit saml.group_mapping.* audit events.

story: As an org admin, I invite an email at a role and review my org's invites.
expected: Org-admin required; invited role may not exceed the inviter's (403). POST returns 201 with the one-time accept_link exactly once (token stored only as hash, never persisted raw) and emailed flag; email send is best-effort — missing RESEND config or send failure never breaks invite creation. GET lists org invites (pending/accepted/expired/revoked) with no tokens. Invite creation rate-limited 20/hour.

story: As an invited user, I redeem the one-time token to join the org at the invited role.
expected: Any authed user (viewer+), kill-switch gated; token is hash-compared and single-use. 400 empty token; 404 unknown/used token; 409 revoked, already-used, or expired; 403 if the invite was issued to a different account/email. Accepting never escalates an existing member's role; returns {org_id, org_role, created} and emits member.joined only when a membership is created.

story: As an org admin, I revoke a pending invite so the link stops working.
expected: Org-admin required, kill-switch gated, org-scoped: 404 if the invite is absent (or belongs to another org), 409 if already accepted; returns the serialized invite with revoked state.

story: As any org member (viewer+), I see my org's members and their org roles.
expected: Org viewer role required; returns only the caller's active org's members — no cross-org leakage; 403 if the caller has no org.

story: As an org admin, I change a member's org role.
expected: Org-admin required, kill-switch gated; 404 if the target is not a member of this org; 409 when demoting the last admin (an org must keep at least one admin). Emits member.role_changed and returns {user_id, org_role}.

story: As an org admin I remove a member, or as any member I leave the org myself.
expected: Route accepts org viewer, but a non-admin removing anyone other than themselves gets 403 {code:'insufficient_org_role'} — self-leave only. 404 if target not a member; 409 if the last admin would be removed or leave. Removal is org-scoped (not account deactivation) and takes effect immediately via membership re-validation; emits member.left/member.removed.

story: As an org admin I list and inspect only my org's users; as a superadmin I see all users platform-wide.
expected: require_org_role(admin): org-admin results are bounded by an INNER JOIN on memberships to ctx.org_id; a user outside the org returns 404 on detail so cross-org existence never leaks. Superadmin sees every user with primary (oldest) membership enriched. List is cursor-paginated (limit 1-100, next_cursor/has_more); detail includes org_role, auth_provider, analysis_count, batch_count.

story: As a platform superadmin, I change a user's global platform role.
expected: Superadmin only: an org-admin gets 403 {code:'platform_superadmin_required'} (org admins manage org_role on the org router, never users.role). 400 changing own role or role not in {viewer, analyst, admin} — 'superadmin' is deliberately not assignable via API; 404 unknown user. Emits user.role_changed with old/new roles.

story: As a platform superadmin, I deactivate a compromised/offboarded account and later reactivate it.
expected: Superadmin only (deliberately not org-admin — deactivation is account-level and blocks EVERY auth path: login, Google/SAML/magic re-provision, existing sessions, API keys). Deactivate: 400 on self, 404 unknown user; flips is_active, sets deactivated_at, and bumps session_version so existing dashboard sessions die immediately. Reactivate reverses it; both idempotent (session_version only bumps on actual state change) and audited.

story: As a platform superadmin, I invalidate every dashboard session for an account without deactivating it.
expected: Superadmin only; 404 unknown user. Bumps users.session_version so every existing dashboard cookie is invalidated on next validation while API keys and the account remain active; returns the new session_version and emits user.sessions_revoked.

story: As an org admin, I see real usage counts for my org's trailing window.
expected: Org-admin required; days param 1-90 (default 30). Returns separate honest counts (analyses, cost_decisions, usage_events, webhook_deliveries) plus per-event-type and per-webhook-status breakdowns from persisted tables — never invented aggregate numbers. Org-admin counts are filtered to ctx.org_id; superadmin is unfiltered (org_id null in response).

story: As an org admin, I inspect recent webhook delivery attempts and retry timing.
expected: Org-admin required; latest deliveries (limit 1-100) joined to batch ULID, org-scoped unless superadmin. Response contains status/attempts/response_code/retry timestamps but deliberately NEVER the payload body.

story: As an org admin/operator, I check async queue, batch, webhook, and worker posture.
expected: Org-admin required; returns PII-free summary scoped to the caller's org (superadmin sees platform-wide, org filter None).

story: As an org admin, I query or CSV-export my org's audit trail for compliance.
expected: Org-admin required; start/end ISO datetimes mandatory (400 on invalid) with a hard 90-day max range (400 above). Org-admin sees only their org's entries, superadmin all orgs. format=csv returns text/csv attachment; default JSON is cursor-paginated (limit 1-200) with optional user_id/action filters.

story: As an IdP (Okta/Entra) using an org-admin API key, I discover the SCIM capabilities.
expected: Bearer API-key auth + org-admin role; a token without an org context gets 403 {code:'scim_org_required'} — SCIM strictly requires an org-scoped admin key. Returns static SCIM 2.0 config/schema/resource-type documents.

story: As an IdP, I list, create, read, replace, and patch users in the customer org.
expected: Org-admin key required; all operations are bounded to the key's org. List supports startIndex/count (max 100) and SCIM filter. POST returns 201 and create_or_update upserts by userName; PUT preserves userName from the existing resource; PATCH requires the SCIM PatchOp schema when schemas is supplied (400 otherwise). Mutations are committed per request.

story: As an IdP, I deprovision a user when they leave the customer's directory.
expected: Org-admin key required; DELETE is implemented as a PATCH setting active=false (soft deactivation, never a hard delete) and returns 204 with no body. Org-scoped — cannot deprovision users outside the key's org.

story: As an IdP, I read and push group membership so directory groups drive org roles.
expected: Org-admin key required; groups are org-scoped, group_id accepts a path segment (:path converter). PATCH applies membership operations and commits; unknown group/org mismatch surfaces the service's error rather than crossing the tenant boundary.

page: Depends(admit_analysis) on POST /validate and sibling compute routes
story: As the platform, I bound in-flight analyses so a burst returns clean retryable 429s instead of DB-pool 500s, and no single org starves the rest.
expected: Beyond MAX_CONCURRENT_ANALYSES (default 8) globally the request gets 429 {code:'server_busy'} with Retry-After; beyond MAX_CONCURRENT_ANALYSES_PER_ORG (default 3) for the caller's org it gets 429 {code:'org_at_capacity'} with Retry-After. Slots are always released in finally even when the analysis fails. Fails OPEN (no-op) for unauthenticated callers, unresolvable membership, or a membership-lookup DB error; ADMISSION_DISABLED bypass works only outside RELEASE — in production the gate cannot be switched off.

story: As an org member, I propose a DRAFT rate-card/shop-profile version for admin review.
expected: Org member+ required; 400 if caller has no org, unknown asset_type, target version not found (404), or target not in 'draft' status (400). On success creates a 'proposed' request, emits an org-scoped admin-audience notification (governance.change_requested), and returns the serialized request. Rate-limited 60/hour.

story: As any org member (viewer+), I browse my org's change requests and open one.
expected: Viewer role required; list is org-scoped newest-first with optional ?status filter and returns an honest empty list when the caller has no org. Detail returns 404 for a missing request, another org's request, or a caller with no org — cross-tenant reads never succeed.

story: As an org admin, I approve a proposed change, which publishes the target draft through the library's own publish path.
expected: Org-admin required; 404 unknown/cross-org request, 409 if the request is not in 'proposed' status. Publishing goes through the library's existing path — a publish failure surfaces that library error and the request is NOT marked approved (fail-closed). Success resolves the pending review notification, emits governance.approved + library.version_published audit events, and returns both the request and the published version.

story: As an org admin, I reject a proposed change with an optional note; the draft stays a draft.
expected: Org-admin required; 404 unknown/cross-org, 409 if not 'proposed'. Rejection never mutates the target draft (it remains draft, nothing published), resolves the review notification, emits governance.rejected, and returns the request in 'rejected' state with the note.

story: As any org member (viewer+), I list my org's notifications with unread/dismissed/status filters.
expected: Viewer role required; org-scoped with per-user read/dismiss state, cursor-paginated (limit 1-100). status must match open|resolved|all; default shows unread non-dismissed; 400 when dismissed=true is combined with unread=true (contradictory). A caller with no org gets an honest empty list, not an error.

story: As any org member, I mark a notification read, dismiss it from my inbox, or restore a dismissed one — affecting only my own view.
expected: Viewer role required; state (read_at/dismissed_at) is per-user, org-scoped — another org's notification id is not reachable. dismiss/restore return 404 when the caller has no org; read no-ops with {ok:true}. Each returns the updated serialized notification.

story: As any org member, I clear my unread badge in one call.
expected: Viewer role required; marks all of the caller's org notifications read for this user only and returns {ok:true, count, read_at}. No-org callers get count 0 with ok:true (honest no-op).

story: As a security reviewer, I verify every API response carries hardening headers without breaking streaming bodies.
expected: Every HTTP response (including streamed CSV exports — pure-ASGI, not buffered) carries Strict-Transport-Security (max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains), X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin, Permissions-Policy disabling camera/mic/geolocation, and Server rewritten to 'ProofShape' (stack never advertised). SECURITY_HEADERS_ENABLED=0 disables it (default on).

story: As an operator debugging an incident, I correlate a client request with logs and Sentry via one ID.
expected: An inbound X-Request-ID header is propagated; absent one, a UUID4 is generated. The ID is echoed back on the response as X-Request-ID, bound into structlog contextvars for every log line of the request, tagged onto the Sentry scope, and unbound after completion.

page: Rate-limit + kill-switch behavior across identity/org/governance/notifications routes
story: As the platform, I throttle each route (e.g. 20/hour onboarding, 20/hour invites, 60/hour governance decisions, 120/hour reads) and gate all mutations behind the global kill-switch.
expected: Exceeding a route's slowapi limit returns 429; every mutating route in orgs/identity onboarding carries Depends(require_kill_switch_open) so writes are refused while the kill-switch is closed, while reads remain available — fail-closed for writes only.

story: As a recipient of a share link, I want to view the DFM analysis without logging in so that I can review the verdict and issues.
expected: Server component fetches the public backend endpoint /s/{shortId} (no auth); renders filename + verdict badge, geometry stat cards (faces, volume cm3, dimensions, watertight — each omitted when absent), issues sorted error>warning>info with codes and fix suggestions, and a process-ranking table sorted by score. A 404/revoked/failed fetch renders 'Analysis not available… may have been revoked by its owner' with a link home. OG metadata is generated from the data; page is noindex; header labels it 'Shared analysis · read-only'.

story: As a supplier or teammate, I want to view a shared should-cost decision without auth so that I see the recommendation with its honesty caveats intact.
expected: Fetches public /s/cost/{shortId}; renders 'Make by <process>' with DFM-ready/needs-redesign badge, a crossover sentence derived from decision.crossover_qty (or 'stays cheapest at every quantity tested', or 'costed but returned no make-vs-buy decision'), the travelling CostHonestyNote, verbatim confidence band (low–high, ±%, validated n or basis), geometry cards, a recommendation-by-quantity table with 'not DFM-ready' badges and 'cheaper if redesigned' alternates, and provenance-tagged assumption chips. Missing/revoked → 'Cost decision not available'. Noindex; footer states 'assumption-based, not a validated quote'.

story: As a visitor, I scroll the home page and see the five-act WebGL part story (hero, routed, glass box, assembly, $14.14 number, close) with captions fading in per section.
